title: PR gating: probabilistic forecasting-based performance regression harness
creator: Aisha Malik
description: Goal: Replace brittle threshold-only PR gates with a probabilistic, time-series forecasting harness that predicts expected p95 tokens/sec (and variance) for a given benchmark slice and flags likely regressions before they become persistent. This ticket implements an end-to-end prototype: 1) collect compact rolling metrics from CI runs; 2) train lightweight forecasting models per-slice; 3) compute prediction intervals and z-scores; 4) surface a graded PR outcome (allow, warn, fail) and attach evidence to PRs.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype forecasting pipeline produces a 90% prediction interval for p95 tokens/sec with historical coverage >= 88% on 6-week test data
CI harness integrates forecasting step and annotates PRs with forecast vs observed delta + confidence interval
PR gating policy implemented: warn below 1.25 sigma, fail at >= 2.5 sigma after corroborating microburst probe
Dashboard widget demonstrates detection latency, false positive rate, and per-slice operating characteristics
design_notes: Approach and trade-offs: start with deterministic, fast models (EWMA + seasonality adjustment) as a baseline and compare to a Prophet-style additive model in the spike. We conservatively choose per-slice models scoped by (model-family, sequence-length-bucket, route) to keep state manageable. Prediction intervals are estimated via quantile regression on residuals (bootstrap initially). To lower false positives, require an orthogonal corroboration signal: a short synthetic microburst probe (20s, three runs) that targets the same slice on a warmed cache. If both forecast z-score and microburst delta exceed configured thresholds, the gate will fail.
implementation_plan: 1) Ingest: extend ci-metrics-exporter to emit a compact time series (p95 tokens/sec, p50, sample count) per-benchmark-slice to a short-term TSDB (7d retention) used by forecasting; 2) Model service: lightweight Python service in CI that loads last N points, fits EWMA + seasonal correction and returns point forecast + 90/95% intervals; 3) CI integration: bench-runner step that calls model service before/after run and posts annotation to PR with a small artifact (json evidence); 4) Microburst probe: a short driver implemented in bench-runner that runs with identical prompt mixes; 5) Dashboard + monitoring: Grafana panel and alerting for false positive spikes.
decisions_and_tradeoffs:
- Accuracy vs latency: prefer sub-10s forecast latency for CI responsiveness. Complex deep models (LSTM) deferred to follow-up.
- Per-slice granularity chosen to reduce cross-workload leakage; increases number of models but keeps error interpretable.
- Conservative gating policy to avoid developer friction: WARN first, FAIL only when corroborated.
- Initial bootstrap uses offline historical residual sampling rather than full Bayesian posterior due to engineering velocity.
risks:
- Risk of noisy baselines for low-sample slices (rare models/long tails) causing false positives. Mitigation: fall back to family-level baselines with higher variance and label PR as low-confidence.
- CI runtime overhead: additional calls to model service and microburst probes will add ~30-60s to some PR checks. Mitigation: parallelize microburst where possible; only run microburst on suspicious diffs.
- Storage cost for per-slice time series — limit retention and compact metrics to reduce storage.
test_plan:
- Offline evaluation on 12 weeks of CI history: compute detection ROC across a labeled set of injected regressions (synthetic -5% to -40% p95). Report AUC and operating points.
- Live canary: enable as WARN only on the bench-runner smoke job for 10% of PRs for two weeks and track FP/FN.
- After canary, flip to WARN for all PRs and run microburst corroboration in background for 2 weeks before any FAIL rollout.
